title.zh: 卷366 列傳一百五十三 孙玉庭 蒋攸铦 李鸿宾
title.en: Volume 366 Biographies 153: Sun Yuting, Jiang Youxian, Li Hongbin
title.raw: 卷366 列傳一百五十三 孙玉庭 蒋攸铦 李鸿宾

sentences.zh: 列傳一百五十三

translations.literal: Biography 153
translations.idiomatic: Biography 153

sentences.zh: 孫玉庭、蔣攸銛、李鴻賓

translations.literal: Sun Yuting, Jiang Youxian, and Li Hongbin
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuting, Jiang Youxian, and Li Hongbin

sentences.zh: 孫玉庭，字寄圃，山東濟寧人。

translations.literal: Sun Yuting, styled Jipu, was a native of Jining in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuting, courtesy name Jipu, came from Jining in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor in the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the fortieth year of the Qianlong reign, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and received an appointment as reviser.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，出為山西河東道，父憂去，服闋，補廣西鹽法道。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he went out as intendant of Hedong circuit in Shanxi; he left on his father's death, and after mourning was assigned to the Guangxi salt administration circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he was posted as intendant of the Hedong circuit in Shanxi. He left office to observe mourning for his father, and when the mourning period ended he was assigned to the Guangxi salt administration circuit.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，就遷按察使，歷湖南、安徽、湖北布政使，舉發道員胡齊崙侵冒軍需，詔嘉之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiaqing he was promoted in place to provincial judicial commissioner, served successively as financial commissioner of Hunan, Anhui, and Hubei, and exposed the circuit intendant Hu Qilun for embezzling military supplies; an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiaqing reign he was promoted in place to provincial judicial commissioner, then served in turn as financial commissioner of Hunan, Anhui, and Hubei. When he exposed the circuit intendant Hu Qilun for embezzling military supplies, the throne commended him by edict.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢廣西巡撫，調廣東。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to governor of Guangxi and transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to governor of Guangxi and soon transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 安南國王阮光纘為農耐、阮福映所逼，叩關乞內避，命玉庭馳赴廣西察辦。

translations.literal: The king of Annam, Nguyen Quang Toan, being pressed by Nong Nai and Nguyen Phuc Anh, knocked at the border gate begging to enter for refuge; Yuting was ordered to hurry to Guangxi to investigate and handle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Annamese king Nguyen Quang Toan, hard pressed by Nong Nai and Nguyen Phuc Anh, came to the border seeking refuge within the empire. Sun Yuting was ordered to proceed posthaste to Guangxi to investigate.

sentences.zh: 福映已滅光纘，遣使納款，玉庭疏陳其恭順，請受之。

translations.literal: Phuc Anh had already destroyed Quang Toan and sent envoys to submit; Yuting memorialized that he was respectful and submissive and asked to accept him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Phuc Anh had overthrown Quang Toan and sent envoys to offer submission. Sun Yuting memorialized that his conduct was respectful and submissive and urged the court to accept him.

sentences.zh: 尋福映請改國名曰南越，仁宗疑之。

translations.literal: Soon Phuc Anh asked to change the state name to Nanyue, and the Jiaqing Emperor was doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Phuc Anh asked to change his state's name to Nanyue, which made the Jiaqing Emperor uneasy.

sentences.zh: 玉庭言：「不可以語言文字阻外夷鄉化之心。

translations.literal: Yuting said: "One must not use language and writing to obstruct the desire of outer barbarians to turn toward civilization.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuting argued: "We must not let quibbles over names and script stand in the way of a foreign state's wish to draw nearer to civilization.

sentences.zh: 其先有古越裳地，繼並安南。

translations.literal: They formerly had the land of ancient Yueshang, and later annexed Annam.
translations.idiomatic: Their ancestors once held the lands of ancient Yueshang and later united Annam under their rule.

sentences.zh: 若改號越南，亦與中國南粵舊名有別。

translations.literal: If the title is changed to Yuenan, it is also distinct from the old name of China's Southern Yue.
translations.idiomatic: If the state is renamed Yuenan, that title is still distinct from the old Chinese name Southern Yue.

sentences.zh: 」乃報可。

translations.literal: " Approval was reported.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 廣東海盜日橫，玉庭議防急於剿，請增兵嚴守口岸，禁淡水米糧出海以製之。

translations.literal: Pirates in Guangdong grew daily more rampant; Yuting argued that defense was more urgent than suppression, asked to increase troops and strictly guard the ports, and forbade fresh water, rice, and grain from going out to sea to restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Piracy in Guangdong grew worse by the day. Sun Yuting argued that defense should take priority over pursuit, asked for more troops to hold the ports tightly, and proposed cutting off supplies of fresh water, rice, and grain at sea to bring the pirates to heel.

sentences.zh: 尋調廣西，十年，復調廣東。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Guangxi; in the tenth year he was again transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Guangxi, and in the tenth year returned to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 時總督那彥成專意招撫，玉庭意不合，疏陳其弊，謂：「盜非悔罪，特為貪利而來。

translations.literal: At the time Governor-General Nayancheng devoted himself solely to pacification by enticement; Yuting disagreed and memorialized on its abuses, saying: "The bandits are not repenting of crime but come solely for profit.
translations.idiomatic: The governor-general Nayancheng was then devoted entirely to winning pirates over by inducement. Sun Yuting disagreed and memorialized on the abuses of that policy, writing: "The bandits are not repenting of their crimes; they come only for gain.

sentences.zh: 官吏貪功，不惜重金為市。

translations.literal: Officials, greedy for merit, do not spare heavy gold as the price.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for credit, officials do not hesitate to pay huge sums to buy them off.

sentences.zh: 陽避盜名，陰攖盜實。

translations.literal: Outwardly they avoid the name of banditry, inwardly they abet the bandits' substance.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly they shun the stigma of banditry while secretly sustaining the bandits in fact.

sentences.zh: 廢法斂怨，莫此為尤。

translations.literal: To abandon the law and gather resentment—nothing is worse than this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing breeds public resentment more than casting aside the law in this way.

sentences.zh: 」上韙其言，那彥成由是獲罪。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words, and Nayancheng thereby incurred guilt.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor endorsed his view, and Nayancheng was punished as a result.

sentences.zh: 十三年，英吉利兵船入澳門，總督吳熊光但停貿易，未遣兵驅逐，上斥畏葸，罷熊光，調玉庭貴州。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year English warships entered Macao; Governor Wu Xiongguang only halted trade and did not send troops to drive them away; the emperor rebuked his timidity, dismissed Xiongguang, and transferred Yuting to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year British warships entered Macao. Governor Wu Xiongguang merely suspended trade and sent no troops to expel them. The emperor denounced his timidity, removed him from office, and transferred Sun Yuting to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋百齡至粵，追論熊光，且劾玉庭不以實入告，坐罷歸。

translations.literal: Soon Bailin arrived in Guangdong, pursued the case against Xiongguang, and also impeached Yuting for not reporting the facts, whereupon he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Bailin arrived in Guangdong, reopened the case against Wu Xiongguang, and also impeached Sun Yuting for failing to report the facts truthfully. Sun Yuting was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 已而予官編修，在文穎館行走。

translations.literal: Before long he was given the post of compiler and served in the Wenyin Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to the rank of Hanlin compiler and assigned to duty in the Wenyin Hall.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授雲南巡撫，兼署雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed governor of Yunnan and concurrently acted as governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed governor of Yunnan and concurrently served as acting governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 調浙江。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 二十年，英吉利貢使不原行跪拜禮，廷議以其倔強，遣之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the English tribute envoy was unwilling to perform the kowtow; the court debated and, deeming him obstinate, sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year the British tribute envoy refused to perform the kowtow. The court judged him obstinate and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 會玉庭入覲，面奏馭夷之道：「妄有乾求，當折以天朝之法度；

translations.literal: When Yuting came to audience, he memorialized in person on the way to manage barbarians: "If they presumptuously make demands, they should be checked by the statutes of the Celestial Dynasty;
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Yuting came to court for audience, he explained in person how to manage foreign powers: "If they presumptuously press demands, they should be checked by the laws of the dynasty;

sentences.zh: 歸心恪順，不責以中國之儀文。

translations.literal: if their hearts return in respectful submission, do not demand of them China's ritual forms."
translations.idiomatic: but if their hearts are truly submissive, do not insist on Chinese ritual forms."

sentences.zh: 」反覆開陳，上意乃解。

translations.literal: He set this forth repeatedly, and the emperor's mind was thereby eased.
translations.idiomatic: He explained this again and again until the emperor's mind was set at ease.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，調兩江。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 漕、鹽、河為江南要政，日臻疲累。

translations.literal: Grain transport, salt, and rivers were the chief policies of Jiangnan and grew daily more exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Grain transport, the salt monopoly, and river control were the chief affairs of Jiangnan, and all were growing more strained by the day.

sentences.zh: 玉庭久任封圻，治尚安靜，整頓江西、湖北引岸緝私，籌款生息，津貼屯丁，減省漕委，隨事為補苴之計，稍稍相安。

translations.literal: Yuting had long held frontier posts and favored quiet governance; he put in order the transit banks of Jiangxi and Hubei to suppress smuggling, raised funds to earn interest, subsidized garrison colonists, reduced grain-transport deputies, and wherever possible made patchwork plans, so that things gradually became somewhat settled.
translations.idiomatic: Having long served on provincial frontiers, Sun Yuting favored quiet governance. He tightened control over the salt transit banks of Jiangxi and Hubei to suppress smuggling, raised funds to earn interest, subsidized garrison colonists, and reduced grain-transport deputies. With such piecemeal remedies affairs gradually grew somewhat easier.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，特加太子少保銜。

translations.literal: When the Daoguang Emperor ascended the throne, he was specially given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Daoguang Emperor came to the throne, Sun Yuting was specially granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時用尚書英和言，清查直省陋規，立以限制，下疆臣議久遠之法。

translations.literal: At the time the court followed the advice of Minister Yinghe to investigate irregular fees in all provinces, set limits on them, and order frontier officials to deliberate on a long-term method.
translations.idiomatic: The court then followed Minister Yinghe's advice to investigate irregular local fees throughout the provinces, set limits on them, and order frontier officials to devise a lasting remedy.

sentences.zh: 玉庭疏言：「自古有治人無治法。

translations.literal: Yuting memorialized: "From antiquity there have been men who govern well, not methods that govern well.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuting memorialized: "From antiquity there have been men who govern well, not laws that govern well by themselves.

sentences.zh: 果督撫兩司皆得人，則大法小廉，自不虞所屬苛取病民；

translations.literal: If governors, financial commissioners, and judicial commissioners are all the right men, then great law and small integrity follow of themselves, and one need not fear that subordinates will exact harshly and harm the people;
translations.idiomatic: If governors and the two provincial commissioners are the right men, great principles and small integrity follow of themselves, and there is no need to fear that subordinates will squeeze the people with harsh exactions;

sentences.zh: 非然者，雖立限制，仍同虛設，弊且滋甚。

translations.literal: otherwise, though limits are set up, they are still the same as empty forms, and abuses will grow worse.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise, though limits are imposed, they remain empty forms and abuses only grow worse.

sentences.zh: 各省陋規，本幹例禁。

translations.literal: The irregular fees of each province have always been forbidden by statute in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Such irregular fees have always been forbidden in principle by statute.

sentences.zh: 語云：'作法於涼，其弊猶貪。

translations.literal: The saying goes: 'If one makes law in a lenient spirit, the abuse will still be greed.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, 'If you make law in a lenient spirit, the abuse will still be greed.

sentences.zh: '禁人之取猶不能不取；

translations.literal: ' To forbid others from taking and yet they still cannot but take;
translations.idiomatic: ' Forbid people from taking and they will still take;

sentences.zh: 若許之取，勢必益無顧忌。

translations.literal: if one permits them to take, they will inevitably become all the more reckless.
translations.idiomatic: permit them to take and they will inevitably grow all the more reckless.

sentences.zh: 迨發覺治罪，民已大受其累。

translations.literal: By the time discovery leads to punishment, the people have already suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: By the time abuses are discovered and punished, the people have already suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 府、廳、州、縣祿入無多，向來不能不藉陋規為辦公之需，然未聞准其加取於民垂為令甲者，誠以自古無此制祿之經也。

translations.literal: The salaries of prefectures, subprefectures, departments, and districts are not large; they have always had to rely on irregular fees for office expenses, yet one has never heard of authorizing additional exactions from the people and making them permanent statutes—for truly from antiquity there has been no such classic of fixing salaries in this way.
translations.idiomatic: The formal salaries of prefectures, subprefectures, departments, and districts are small, and officials have long had to rely on irregular fees for office expenses. Yet never before has the throne authorized additional exactions from the people and enshrined them in permanent statute—for from antiquity there has been no such way of fixing official pay.

sentences.zh: 伏乞停止查辦，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: I humbly beg that the investigation be stopped; the realm would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that this investigation be halted; the empire would be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，詔褒其不媿大臣之言。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, an edict praised it as words worthy of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived, an edict praised it as words worthy of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，授協辦大學士，仍留總督任。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was appointed associate grand secretary while retaining his post as governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daoguang he was appointed associate grand secretary while remaining governor-general.

sentences.zh: 是年入覲，與玉瀾堂十五老臣宴。

translations.literal: That year he came to audience and was feasted with the fifteen old ministers in the Yulan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That year he came to court and was feasted with the fifteen senior ministers in the Yulan Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝詢淮鹽疏銷之策，玉庭言：「漢口為淮南售鹽總岸，向來船到隨時交易，是以暢銷。

translations.literal: The emperor asked about measures to improve the sluggish sale of Huai salt; Yuting said: "Hankou is the chief bank for selling Huainan salt; formerly when ships arrived they traded at once, and therefore sales were brisk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked how to revive sluggish sales of Huai salt. Sun Yuting replied: "Hankou is the chief market for Huainan salt. Formerly, when ships arrived they could trade at once, and sales were brisk.

sentences.zh: 自乾隆中立封輪法，挨次輪售，私鹽乘間侵越。

translations.literal: Since the Qianlong reign established the sealed-rotation method, selling in turn by rotation, smuggled salt seized the interval to encroach.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Qianlong reign established the sealed rotation system, with sales taken in strict turn, smuggled salt seized every opening to encroach.

sentences.zh: 」因臚陳六害，請復舊章，從之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon set forth six harms in detail and asked to restore the old regulations; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " He then detailed six harms of the new system and asked to restore the old regulations, which was approved.

sentences.zh: 又言漕糧浮收不能禁革，不如明與八折為便。

translations.literal: He also said that the excess collection on tribute grain could not be forbidden and abolished, and that it would be better to grant an explicit twenty-percent reduction.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the illegal surcharges on tribute grain could not be stamped out, and that it would be better to grant an explicit twenty-percent reduction.

sentences.zh: 御史王家相奏言事類加賦，侍郎姚文田、湯金釗亦論之，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Jiaxiang memorialized that the matter resembled an added levy; Vice Ministers Yao Wentian and Tang Jinshao also debated it, and the affair was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Jiaxiang memorialized that the proposal amounted to a new levy. Vice Ministers Yao Wentian and Tang Jinshao also objected, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 然州縣困於丁費，浮收仍難禁絕，胥吏上下其手，專累良懦，因玉庭議不行，疆臣不敢復請；

translations.literal: Yet districts and counties were strained by labor fees; excess collection was still hard to forbid entirely, clerks manipulated matters above and below, and the honest and weak alone bore the burden. Because Yuting's proposal was not adopted, frontier officials did not dare ask again;
translations.idiomatic: Yet districts and counties remained strained by labor fees, illegal surcharges could still not be stamped out, and clerks manipulated accounts to burden only the honest and weak. Because Sun Yuting's proposal was rejected, frontier officials did not dare raise it again;

sentences.zh: 至同治初，始定漕耗，卒如玉庭議。

translations.literal: only at the beginning of Tongzhi was the grain-transport surcharge fixed, ultimately as Yuting had proposed.
translations.idiomatic: not until the early Tongzhi reign was the grain-transport surcharge fixed—ultimately along the lines Sun Yuting had proposed.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜體仁閣大學士，留任如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Tiren Pavilion and retained his post as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Tiren Pavilion while retaining his post as before.

sentences.zh: 會高家堰決，河督張文浩遣戍，部議玉庭革職，詔念前勞，寬之，留任。

translations.literal: When the Gaojia Weir burst, River Director Zhang Wenhao was banished; the ministry proposed that Yuting be dismissed from office, but an edict, mindful of his former service, showed leniency and kept him in post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaojia Weir burst, River Director Zhang Wenhao was banished. The ministry proposed that Sun Yuting be dismissed, but an edict, mindful of his long service, showed leniency and kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 尋復以借黃濟運無效，褫職，予編修休致。

translations.literal: Soon he was again stripped of office because borrowing Yellow River water to aid transport had failed, and was given the rank of compiler with permission to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again stripped of office because the scheme of borrowing Yellow River water to aid transport had failed, and was granted retirement with the rank of Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 戶部复劾其不行海運，而河病運阻，責償滯漕剝運費十之七，命留濬運河。

translations.literal: The Board of Revenue again impeached him for not implementing sea transport; because the river was sick and transport blocked, he was charged to repay seven-tenths of the fees for delayed tribute and stripped transport costs, and was ordered to remain to dredge the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Revenue again impeached him for failing to implement sea transport. Because the river was failing and transport blocked, he was ordered to repay seven-tenths of the fees for delayed tribute grain and stripped transport costs, and was kept on to dredge the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 工竣，回籍。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, he returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, he returned home.

sentences.zh: 十四年，重宴鹿鳴，加四品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was again feasted at the Luming banquet and given a fourth-rank official button.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was again honored at the Luming banquet and granted a fourth-rank official button.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年八十有三。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward, at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 子善寶，以舉人廕生授刑部員外郎，官至江蘇巡撫；

translations.literal: His son Shanbao, by hereditary privilege as a juren, was appointed a secretary in the Board of Punishments and rose to governor of Jiangsu;
translations.idiomatic: His son Shanbao entered office by hereditary privilege as a juren, served in the Board of Punishments, and rose to governor of Jiangsu;

sentences.zh: 瑞珍，道光三年進士，由翰林官至戶部尚書，諡文定。

translations.literal: Ruizhen, a jinshi of the third year of Daoguang, rose from the Hanlin to Minister of Revenue and was given the posthumous title Wending.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizhen, a jinshi of the third year of Daoguang, rose from the Hanlin to Minister of Revenue and was posthumously titled Wending.

sentences.zh: 孫毓溎，道光二十四年一甲一名進士，官至浙江按察使；

translations.literal: His grandson Yuwen, top graduate of the first rank in the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang, rose to provincial judicial commissioner of Zhejiang;
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yuwen, top graduate of the first rank in the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang, rose to provincial judicial commissioner of Zhejiang;

sentences.zh: 毓汶亦以一甲二名進士，官至兵部尚書，自有傳。

translations.literal: Yuwen also was second graduate of the first rank and rose to Minister of War; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen was second graduate of the first rank and rose to Minister of War; he has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 曾孫楫，咸豐二年進士，翰林院庶吉士，官至順天府尹。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Ji, a jinshi of the second year of Xianfeng and Hanlin bachelor, rose to intendant of Shuntian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Ji, a jinshi of the second year of Xianfeng and Hanlin bachelor, rose to intendant of Shuntian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四世並歷清要，家門之盛，北方士族無與埒焉。

translations.literal: Four generations all held pure and important posts; the splendor of the family had no equal among northern gentry clans.
translations.idiomatic: For four generations they held the empire's choicest offices, and no northern gentry clan could match the family's eminence.

sentences.zh: 蔣攸銛，字礪堂，漢軍鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Jiang Youxian, styled Litang, was a bondservant of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Youxian, courtesy name Litang, was a bondservant of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 先世由浙江遷遼東，從入關，居寶坻。

translations.literal: His ancestors moved from Zhejiang to Liaodong, followed the entry into the Pass, and settled in Baodi.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had moved from Zhejiang to Liaodong, followed the Manchus through the Pass, and settled in Baodi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十九年，成進士，年甫十九，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi at only nineteen, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination at only nineteen, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，遷御史，敢言有聲，受仁宗知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiaqing he was transferred to censor, was outspoken and gained a reputation, and won the Jiaqing Emperor's notice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiaqing reign he was made a censor, gained a reputation for outspokenness, and won the Jiaqing Emperor's notice.

sentences.zh: 五年，出為江西吉南贛道，署按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he went out as intendant of Jinan-Gan circuit in Jiangxi and acted as provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was posted as intendant of the Jinan-Gan circuit in Jiangxi and concurrently served as acting provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八年，廣昌齋匪廖幹用作亂，攸銛率兵平之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Zhai bandit Liao Ganqi raised a revolt in Guangchang; Youxian led troops and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Zhai sect bandit Liao Ganqi rebelled at Guangchang. Jiang Youxian led troops and put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 疆臣上其功，會丁母憂去。

translations.literal: Frontier officials reported his merit, but he happened to leave on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials reported his merit, but he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 十年，特起署廣東惠潮嘉道，歷江西按察使、雲南布政使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was specially recalled to act as intendant of Huichao-Jia circuit in Guangdong, and served successively as judicial commissioner of Jiangxi and financial commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was specially recalled to serve as acting intendant of the Huichao-Jia circuit in Guangdong, then held in turn the posts of provincial judicial commissioner of Jiangxi and financial commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 十四年，調江蘇，就擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Jiangsu and was promoted in place to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Jiangsu and promoted in place to governor.

sentences.zh: 調浙江，擢江南河道總督，以不諳河務辭，詔回原任。

translations.literal: Transferred to Zhejiang, he was promoted to director-general of the Jiangnan waterways but declined on grounds of unfamiliarity with river affairs; an edict ordered him back to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Zhejiang, he was promoted to director-general of the Jiangnan waterways but declined on grounds of unfamiliarity with river affairs. An edict ordered him back to his former post.

sentences.zh: 十六年，擢兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to governor-general of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 嚴於治盜，遴勤幹文武大員駐廣、肇、韶、連諸郡居中之地，分路搜截，飭州縣官赴鄉勸導耆老，使境內不得藏奸，舉劾嚴明，吏皆用命。

translations.literal: Strict in governing bandits, he selected diligent civil and military grandees to station at central points in Guangzhou, Zhaoqing, Shaozhou, and Lianzhou circuits, searched and intercepted by separate routes, ordered district and county officials to go to the countryside to persuade the elders, so that the interior might not harbor villains, and was strict in promotion and impeachment; all officials obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: He was severe in suppressing banditry, posting diligent civil and military officials at central points in Guangzhou, Zhaoqing, Shaozhou, and Lianzhou to search and intercept along separate routes. He ordered district and county magistrates to go into the countryside to persuade elders so that criminals could find no refuge within their jurisdictions. His promotions and impeachments were strict, and officials obeyed.

sentences.zh: 歷擒匪盜七百馀名，自首者許自新，特詔褒獎。

translations.literal: In all he captured more than seven hundred bandits and robbers; those who surrendered were permitted to reform, and a special edict praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: In all he captured more than seven hundred bandits and robbers. Those who surrendered were allowed to reform themselves, and a special edict praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 十八年，應詔陳言，略曰：「我朝累代功德在民，而亂民愍不畏法，變出意外，此皆由於吏治不修所致。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, responding to an edict, he memorialized in summary: "Our dynasty's accumulated merit over generations rests with the people, yet disorderly people pityingly do not fear the law and changes arise unexpectedly—all this comes from failure to repair official governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, responding to an imperial edict, he memorialized in summary: "Our dynasty's merit has accumulated over generations among the people, yet disorderly elements no longer fear the law and upheavals arise unexpectedly. All this stems from the failure to repair official governance.

sentences.zh: 臣觀近日道、府、州、縣，貪酷者少而委靡者多。

translations.literal: Your servant observes that among circuit, prefectural, departmental, and county officials of late, the cruel and greedy are few while the slack and spiritless are many.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that among circuit, prefectural, departmental, and county officials of late, the cruel and greedy are few while the slack and spiritless are many.

sentences.zh: 夫闒冗之釀患，與貪酷等。

translations.literal: Slack incompetence breeds disaster no less than cruelty and greed.
translations.idiomatic: Slack incompetence breeds disaster no less than cruelty and greed.

sentences.zh: 竊以為方今急務，莫先於察吏，而欲振積習，必用破格之勸懲。

translations.literal: Your servant believes that among urgent tasks today none comes before inspecting officials, and to shake off accumulated habits one must use extraordinary rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that among today's urgent tasks none comes before inspecting officials, and to shake off entrenched habits one must use extraordinary rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 凡貪酷者固應嚴參，平庸者亦隨時勒休改用，勿俟大計始行覈辦。

translations.literal: All who are cruel and greedy should of course be strictly impeached; the mediocre should also be compelled to retire and be reassigned at any time, and not wait until the triennial evaluation to be handled.
translations.idiomatic: The cruel and greedy should of course be strictly impeached, but mediocre officials should also be compelled to retire and be reassigned at any time rather than waiting for the triennial evaluation.

sentences.zh: 其有勤能者，即請旨優獎。

translations.literal: Those who are diligent and capable should at once be specially rewarded by imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Those who are diligent and capable should at once receive special rewards by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 果道、府、州、縣得人，則禍亂之萌自息。

translations.literal: If circuit, prefectural, departmental, and county posts truly get the right men, the sprouts of calamity and disorder will cease of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If circuit, prefectural, departmental, and county posts truly get the right men, the seeds of calamity and disorder will die away of themselves.

sentences.zh: 」次年，又上疏曰：「道府由牧令起家者十之二三，由部員外擢者十之七八。

translations.literal: " The next year he again memorialized: "Of circuit and prefectural officials, two or three in ten rise from magistrates, and seven or eight in ten are promoted from ministry secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: " The next year he memorialized again: "Of circuit and prefectural officials, only two or three in ten rise from magistrates, while seven or eight in ten are promoted from ministry secretaries.

sentences.zh: 聞近來司員少卓著之才，由於滿洲之廕生太易，漢員之捐班太多。

translations.literal: I hear that of late ministry clerks rarely show outstanding talent, because Manchu hereditary privilege is too easy and Han purchase of office is too numerous.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that ministry clerks of late rarely show outstanding talent, because Manchu hereditary privilege is too easy and Han purchase of office too common.

sentences.zh: 請飭部臣隨時考覈，其不宜於部務者，以同知、通判分發各省，使練民事，部曹亦可疏通。

translations.literal: I ask that ministry officials be ordered to examine them at all times; those unsuited to ministry work should be distributed to the provinces as subprefects and assistant prefects to gain practice in civil affairs, and the ministry bureaus may also be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that ministry officials examine them regularly. Those unsuited to ministry work should be sent to the provinces as subprefects and assistant prefects to gain experience in civil affairs, which would also relieve congestion in the ministries.

sentences.zh: 今之人才沉於下位者多矣，請飭大臣薦達，擇其名實相副者擢用。

translations.literal: Much talent today is sunk in low posts; I ask that great ministers be ordered to recommend and advance men, selecting those whose reputation and reality match for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Much talent today languishes in low posts. I ask that senior ministers be ordered to recommend men whose reputation and ability truly match for promotion.

sentences.zh: 抑臣更有請者，任事之與專擅，有義利之分，若任事而以專擅罪之，人皆推諉以自全矣。

translations.literal: Moreover your servant has another request: between taking responsibility for affairs and acting on one's own authority there is a distinction of right and profit; if one is punished for taking responsibility as though it were usurpation, everyone will shirk duty to preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: I have another request. Between taking responsibility and acting on one's own authority there is a distinction of right and expedience. If officials are punished for taking responsibility as though it were usurpation, everyone will shirk duty to preserve himself.

sentences.zh: 協恭之與黨援，有公私之別，如協恭而以黨援目之，人且立異以遠嫌矣。

translations.literal: Between harmonious cooperation and factional patronage there is a distinction of public and private; if harmonious cooperation is viewed as factional patronage, people will set themselves apart to avoid suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Between harmonious cooperation and factional patronage there is a distinction of public and private interest. If cooperation is treated as factional patronage, people will set themselves apart to avoid suspicion.

sentences.zh: 此近今之積習，為大臣者當力除之。

translations.literal: These are accumulated habits of recent times; great ministers should strive to remove them.
translations.idiomatic: These are entrenched habits of recent times, and great ministers should strive to remove them.

sentences.zh: 至翰林儒臣，務在崇正學，黜浮華，養成明體達用之才，不必以文章課殿最。

translations.literal: As for Hanlin scholar-officials, the task lies in honoring orthodox learning, dismissing flashy display, and nurturing talent that understands fundamental principles and can apply them, without necessarily ranking them by literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: As for Hanlin scholar-officials, the task is to honor orthodox learning, dismiss flashy display, and nurture talent that grasps fundamental principles and can apply them—not necessarily to rank them by literary composition alone.

sentences.zh: 科道為耳目之官，敷陳能否得體，糾劾是否為公，詢事考言，難逃洞鑑。

translations.literal: Censors and remonstrators are the eyes and ears of the throne; whether their presentations are appropriate, whether their impeachments are public-spirited—inquiring into affairs and testing words, none escapes penetrating scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and remonstrators are the eyes and ears of the throne. Whether their presentations are appropriate and their impeachments public-spirited—inquiring into affairs and testing words—none escapes penetrating scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 其有卓越清正者，當由京堂而擢卿貳，與翰詹參用。

translations.literal: Those who are outstanding and upright should be promoted from metropolitan department heads to vice ministers and used together with Hanlin and academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Those who are outstanding and upright should be promoted from metropolitan department heads to vice ministers and employed together with Hanlin scholars.

sentences.zh: 用人之道，因才因地因時，臣下無可市之恩，君上有特操之鑑。

translations.literal: The way of employing men depends on talent, place, and time; subordinates have no favor to trade, and the sovereign has a special mirror of judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The way to employ men depends on talent, place, and time. Subordinates have no favors to trade, and the sovereign has his own mirror of judgment.

sentences.zh: 人無求備，政在集思，此之謂也。

translations.literal: One does not demand completeness in men; government lies in gathering counsel—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: One does not demand perfection in every man; government lies in gathering counsel from many minds. That is the point.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived, the emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 英吉利兵船入內洋，攸銛飭停貿易，乃聽命引去。

translations.literal: English warships entered the inner sea; Youxian ordered trade halted, and they then obeyed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When British warships entered the inner sea, Jiang Youxian ordered trade halted, and they then withdrew as instructed.

sentences.zh: 請禁民人為洋人服役，洋行不許建洋式房屋，鋪商不得用洋字店號，清查商欠，不准無身家者濫充洋商，及內地人私往洋館，並如議行。

translations.literal: He asked to forbid the people from serving foreigners, forbid foreign firms from building Western-style houses, forbid shops from using foreign characters in their signs, investigate commercial debts, forbid men without property from recklessly filling foreign merchant posts, and forbid inland people from privately visiting foreign quarters—all were carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed forbidding Chinese from serving foreigners, forbidding foreign firms from building Western-style houses, forbidding shops from using foreign characters in their signs, investigating commercial debts, barring men without property from serving as foreign merchants, and forbidding inland people from visiting foreign quarters privately. All these measures were adopted.

sentences.zh: 商人負暹羅國貨價，以官錢代償，既而貢使來繳還。

translations.literal: Merchants owed the price of Siam's goods; official funds were used to pay on their behalf, and later the tribute envoy came to repay.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants owed payment for Siamese goods, and official funds were used to cover the debt. Later the Siamese tribute envoy came to repay it.

sentences.zh: 攸銛以奉旨頒給，乃示懷柔，不得復收回，卻之，詔嘉其得體。

translations.literal: Youxian argued that since it had been bestowed by imperial order as a display of kindness, it could not be taken back; he refused it, and an edict praised his tact.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Youxian argued that since the payment had been bestowed by imperial order as a gesture of kindness, it could not be taken back. He refused the repayment, and an edict praised his tact.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，調四川總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 四川兵故驕縱，一裁以法。

translations.literal: The troops of Sichuan had long been arrogant and unruly; he cut them all down to law.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan troops had long been arrogant and unruly; he brought them all under strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 民多帶刀劍，禁鄉村設爐制兵刃。

translations.literal: The people commonly carried swords; he forbade villages from setting up furnaces to make weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Because the people commonly carried swords, he forbade villages from setting up furnaces to forge weapons.

sentences.zh: 城市編牌取結，有犯連坐。

translations.literal: In cities he organized household registers and bonds; offenders were punished by joint liability.
translations.idiomatic: In cities he organized household registers and mutual bonds, with joint punishment for offenders.

sentences.zh: 以義倉租息助灌縣都江堰歲修，禁派捐累民。

translations.literal: He used the interest from charity granaries to assist the annual repairs of the Dujiangyan at Guanxian and forbade levies that burdened the people.
translations.idiomatic: He used interest from charity granaries to help fund annual repairs of the Dujiangyan at Guanxian and forbade levies that burdened the people.

sentences.zh: 重修文翁石室，興學造士。

translations.literal: He rebuilt the Stone Chamber of Lord Wen and promoted learning to nurture scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the Stone Chamber of Lord Wen and promoted learning to nurture scholars.

sentences.zh: 言官請禁非刑，飭屬銷毀違法刑具，而嚴戒縱匪，不得博寬厚虛名，貽閭閻實害。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials asked to forbid illegal torture; he ordered subordinates to destroy unlawful instruments of punishment, and strictly warned against indulging bandits or seeking a false reputation for leniency that would bring real harm to the neighborhoods.
translations.idiomatic: When remonstrating officials asked to forbid illegal torture, he ordered subordinates to destroy unlawful instruments of punishment. He also strictly warned against indulging bandits or seeking a false reputation for leniency that would bring real harm to the people.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，率土司頭目入都祝嘏，賞賚有加。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he led native chieftains into the capital to offer congratulations; rewards were especially generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he led native chieftains to the capital to offer congratulations, and they received especially generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 時因慶典，普免天下積欠錢糧，獨四川無欠可免，詔嘉其撫綏有方，予優敘。

translations.literal: At the time, because of a celebration, accumulated tax arrears throughout the realm were generally remitted; Sichuan alone had no arrears to remit, and an edict praised his effective pacification and granted him preferential recognition.
translations.idiomatic: Because of a celebration, accumulated tax arrears throughout the empire were generally remitted. Sichuan alone had no arrears to remit. An edict praised his effective governance and granted him preferential recognition.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，仁宗崩，入謁梓宮，宣宗諭褒為守兼優，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the Jiaqing Emperor died; he entered to pay respects at the coffin, and the Daoguang Emperor praised him as excellent in both defense and administration, adding the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the Jiaqing Emperor died. Jiang Youxian went to pay respects at the coffin, and the Daoguang Emperor praised him as excellent in both defense and administration, granting him the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，召授刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he was summoned and appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daoguang he was summoned to court and appointed Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 尋授直隸總督。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor-general of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 值水災，請截南漕四十萬石，賑款先後二百萬兩，逾年賑事竣。

translations.literal: When floods struck, he asked to divert four hundred thousand shi of southern tribute grain and disbursed two million taels in relief in all; after more than a year the relief work was finished.
translations.idiomatic: When floods struck, he asked to divert four hundred thousand shi of southern tribute grain and disbursed two million taels in relief. After more than a year the relief work was finished.

sentences.zh: 時方治畿輔水利，命侍郎張文浩蒞其事，尋以程含章代之，攸銛與合疏言東西兩淀，大清、永定、子牙、南北運五河，及天津海口、千里堤，不可緩之工，請部撥銀一百二十萬兩；

translations.literal: At the time waterworks in the capital region were under way; Vice Minister Zhang Wenhao was ordered to oversee them and was soon replaced by Cheng Hanzhang. Youxian jointly memorialized that the eastern and western marshes, the Daqing, Yongding, Ziya, and north and south transport rivers, the Tianjin estuary, and the Thousand-Li Dike were works that could not be delayed, and asked the ministry to allocate 1.2 million taels;
translations.idiomatic: Waterworks in the capital region were then under way. Vice Minister Zhang Wenhao was ordered to oversee them and was soon replaced by Cheng Hanzhang. Jiang Youxian jointly memorialized that work on the eastern and western marshes, the Daqing, Yongding, Ziya, and north and south transport rivers, the Tianjin estuary, and the Thousand-Li Dike could not be delayed, and asked the ministry to allocate 1.2 million taels;

sentences.zh: 又疏陳千里堤章程，規复兩淀垡船汊夫，移改管河員弁駐所，添建巡防堡房。

translations.literal: He also memorialized regulations for the Thousand-Li Dike, planned to restore marsh boats and channel laborers in the two marshes, moved the stations of river officials and officers, and added patrol forts and houses.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized regulations for the Thousand-Li Dike, proposing to restore marsh boats and channel laborers, relocate river officials and officers, and add patrol forts and houses.

sentences.zh: 並如議行。

translations.literal: All were carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: All were carried out as proposed.

sentences.zh: 命協辦大學士，仍留總督任。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as associate grand secretary while retaining his post as governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed associate grand secretary while retaining his post as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜體仁閣大學士，充軍機大臣，管理刑部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Tiren Pavilion, served as Grand Council minister, and administered the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Tiren Pavilion, served on the Grand Council, and administered the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 以回疆平，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Because the Muslim frontier was pacified, he was given the title Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Muslim frontier was pacified, he was granted the title Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 七年，授兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 疏言總督於河務非專責，與河臣同治，徒掣其肘，請毋庸駐清江浦​​，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the governor-general had no exclusive responsibility for river affairs and that governing together with the river director only hampered him; he asked not to be required to reside at Qingjiangpu, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the governor-general had no exclusive responsibility for river affairs and that governing jointly with the river director only hampered effective action. He asked not to be required to reside at Qingjiangpu, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 時清水不能敵黃，漕運屢阻。

translations.literal: At the time clear water could not overcome the Yellow River, and grain transport was repeatedly blocked.
translations.idiomatic: At the time clear water could not overcome the Yellow River current, and grain transport was repeatedly blocked.

sentences.zh: 攸銛初在浙，不主海運，至是見河、漕交困，試行海運便利，遂請續行，並預儲銀六十萬兩，備河運盤壩之用。

translations.literal: Youxian had earlier in Zhejiang not favored sea transport; now seeing rivers and grain transport alike in distress, he found trial sea transport convenient and therefore asked to continue it, and also set aside six hundred thousand taels in advance for use in river transport and dam transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Youxian had earlier opposed sea transport while in Zhejiang, but now, seeing both rivers and grain transport in distress, he found trial sea transport effective and asked to continue it. He also set aside six hundred thousand taels in advance for river transport and dam-transfer expenses.

sentences.zh: 廷議方主倒塘濟運法，且疑其畏難便私，不許。

translations.literal: Court debate then favored the method of reversing embankments to aid transport and also suspected him of shirking difficulty for private convenience; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Court debate then favored reversing embankments to aid transport and suspected him of shirking difficulty for private convenience. The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 攸銛疏辯，極言倒塘之不足恃，上終不以為然，姑許海運，而禁言盤壩。

translations.literal: Youxian memorialized in defense, stating at length that reversing embankments could not be relied on; the emperor ultimately did not agree, provisionally permitted sea transport, but forbade discussion of dam transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Youxian memorialized in defense, arguing at length that reversing embankments could not be relied on. The emperor remained unconvinced, provisionally permitted sea transport, but forbade further discussion of dam transfer.

sentences.zh: 未幾，海運亦罷。

translations.literal: Before long sea transport was also abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long sea transport was abandoned as well.

sentences.zh: 以張格爾就擒，追論贊畫功，晉太子太傅。

translations.literal: Because Jahangir was captured, his planning merit was reviewed and he was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jahangir was captured, his planning merit was recognized and he was promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 黃玉林者，鹽梟巨魁，以儀徵老虎頸為窟穴，長江千里，呼吸皆通，詔責嚴捕，玉林投首，乞捕私自效。

translations.literal: Huang Yulin was a great salt-smuggling chieftain who used Laohujing at Yizheng as his lair; along a thousand li of the Yangzi his communications were complete. An edict ordered strict capture; Yulin surrendered and begged to serve by capturing smugglers privately.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yulin was a great salt-smuggling chieftain who used Laohujing at Yizheng as his lair. Along a thousand li of the Yangzi his network was complete. When an edict ordered his capture, Yulin surrendered and offered to hunt smugglers on the government's behalf.

sentences.zh: 十年，攸銛病，乞假，假滿，召回京供職，而玉林复圖販私，攸銛疏請嚴治，發遣新疆，尋复慮其潛回滋事，密請處絞。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Youxian fell ill and asked leave; when leave ended he was recalled to the capital to serve, but Yulin again plotted smuggling. Youxian memorialized asking strict punishment, banishment to Xinjiang, and soon again feared he might slip back and cause trouble and secretly asked that he be executed by strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Jiang Youxian fell ill and took leave. When his leave ended he was recalled to the capital, but Yulin again took up smuggling. Jiang Youxian memorialized for strict punishment and banishment to Xinjiang, then secretly asked that he be executed, fearing he might slip back and cause trouble.

sentences.zh: 詔誅玉林，切責攸銛苟且從事，嚴議褫職，加恩降兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: An edict executed Yulin, sharply rebuked Youxian for perfunctory handling, and after strict deliberation stripped him of office, but as a grace reduced him to vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yulin executed and sharply rebuked Jiang Youxian for perfunctory handling. After strict deliberation he was stripped of office but, as a grace, reduced to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 未至京，卒於途，優詔軫惜，依尚書例賜卹。

translations.literal: Before reaching the capital he died on the road; a gracious edict expressed sorrow, and he was granted funeral honors according to the precedent for ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Before reaching the capital he died on the road. A gracious edict expressed sorrow, and he was granted funeral honors according to the precedent for ministers.

sentences.zh: 攸銛精敏強識，與人一面一言，閱數十年記憶不爽。

translations.literal: Youxian was keen, sharp, and possessed a strong memory; after one meeting and one remark with a person, even decades later his memory did not err.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Youxian was keen and possessed a formidable memory. After a single meeting and a single remark, he could recall a person accurately even decades later.

sentences.zh: 勇於任事，不唯阿。

translations.literal: He was bold in taking responsibility and did not merely agree.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold in taking responsibility and did not merely agree with others.

sentences.zh: 尤長於察吏，薦賢如不及，所舉後多以事功名節著。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at inspecting officials and recommended the worthy as if he could not keep up; those he recommended later often became famous for achievement, reputation, and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at judging officials and recommended the worthy as if he could not do so fast enough. Many of those he promoted later became famous for achievement, reputation, and integrity.

sentences.zh: 子霨遠，官至貴州巡撫，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Wuyuan rose to governor of Guizhou and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wuyuan rose to governor of Guizhou and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 李鴻賓，字鹿蘋，江西德化人。

translations.literal: Li Hongbin, styled Luping, was a native of Dehua in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongbin, courtesy name Luping, came from Dehua in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Jiaqing, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the sixth year of the Jiaqing reign, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 遷御史、給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor and supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to censor and supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 十八年，巡視東漕。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he inspected the eastern grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he inspected the eastern grain transport route.

sentences.zh: 會林清之變，數疏陳時政利弊；

translations.literal: At the time of Lin Qing's rebellion he repeatedly memorialized on the advantages and harms of current policy;
translations.idiomatic: At the time of Lin Qing's rebellion he repeatedly memorialized on the strengths and failings of current policy;

sentences.zh: 又以山東、河南、直隸毗連之地，頻年遭兵，條上善後事，始受仁宗知。

translations.literal: and because Shandong, Henan, and Zhili were adjoining regions that had suffered warfare for years, he set forth items on post-disaster measures and first won the Jiaqing Emperor's notice.
translations.idiomatic: and because Shandong, Henan, and Zhili were adjoining regions that had suffered warfare for years, he set forth measures for recovery. Only then did he win the Jiaqing Emperor's notice.

sentences.zh: 命偕河督吳璥、巡撫同興按河督李亨特貪劣不職狀，得實以聞。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with River Director Wu Jing and Governor Tongxing to investigate River Director Li Hengte's greedy and incompetent conduct; the facts were established and reported.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered, together with River Director Wu Jing and Governor Tongxing, to investigate River Director Li Hengte's greed and incompetence. The charges were substantiated and reported.

sentences.zh: 十九年，超授東河副總河。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was exceptionally appointed deputy director-general of the Eastern Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was exceptionally appointed deputy director-general of the Eastern Rivers.

sentences.zh: 時微山湖蓄水盡涸，運河淤塞。

translations.literal: At the time the stored water of Weishan Lake was entirely exhausted and the Grand Canal silted up.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the stored water of Weishan Lake was entirely exhausted and the Grand Canal silted up.

sentences.zh: 鴻賓自巡漕時講求疏泉濟運之策，至是疏瀹上游，湖水通暢，瀦蓄充盈，漕運無阻，被褒獎，命赴睢工，會同吳璥塞河。

translations.literal: Hongbin had since his grain-transport inspection studied measures to dredge springs and aid transport; now he dredged the upper reaches, the lake water flowed freely, storage was full, and grain transport was unimpeded. He was praised and ordered to the Sui works to join Wu Jing in blocking the river.
translations.idiomatic: Since his grain-transport inspection Li Hongbin had studied measures to dredge springs and aid transport. Now he dredged the upper reaches until lake water flowed freely, storage was full, and grain transport was unimpeded. He was praised and ordered to the Sui works to join Wu Jing in blocking the river.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢河東河道總督。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to director-general of the Hedong waterways.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was promoted to director-general of the Hedong waterways.

sentences.zh: 由諫官不三年而膺方面，為時所罕。

translations.literal: From remonstrating official to frontier post in less than three years was rare in his time.
translations.idiomatic: To rise from remonstrating official to frontier governor in less than three years was rare in his day.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，賜金治喪，予諭祭，異數也。

translations.literal: Soon he left on his mother's death; gold was granted for the funeral and an imperial message of condolence was sent—an extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left office to mourn his mother. Gold was granted for the funeral and an imperial message of condolence was sent—an extraordinary honor.

sentences.zh: 服闋，署禮部、兵部侍郎，命赴河南、山東讞獄，並察黃河、運河、湖水情形。

translations.literal: After mourning he acted as vice minister of rites and war and was ordered to go to Henan and Shandong to judge cases and also inspect conditions on the Yellow River, Grand Canal, and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he served as acting vice minister of rites and war and was ordered to go to Henan and Shandong to judge cases and inspect conditions on the Yellow River, Grand Canal, and lakes.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，署廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he acted as governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he served as acting governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，授漕運總督，復調河東河道總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed director-general of grain transport and was again transferred to director-general of the Hedong waterways.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed director-general of grain transport and was again transferred to director-general of the Hedong waterways.

sentences.zh: 河決蘭陽、儀封，命偕尚書吳璥治之，鴻賓專駐儀封。

translations.literal: The river burst at Lanyang and Yifeng; he was ordered together with Minister Wu Jing to manage it, and Hongbin was stationed specially at Yifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When the river burst at Lanyang and Yifeng, he was ordered to manage the crisis together with Minister Wu Jing, with Li Hongbin stationed at Yifeng.

sentences.zh: 會北岸馬營壩復決，合疏言馬營土質沙松，河溜尚勁，未能遽定壩基，被詰責，遂自陳不胜河督之任。

translations.literal: When the Maying embankment on the north bank burst again, they jointly memorialized that Maying's soil was sandy and loose and the current still strong, so the embankment base could not quickly be fixed; they were rebuked, and Hongbin then confessed himself unequal to the post of river director.
translations.idiomatic: When the Maying embankment on the north bank burst again, they jointly memorialized that the soil there was sandy and loose and the current still strong, so the embankment could not quickly be stabilized. After rebuke Li Hongbin confessed himself unequal to the post of river director.

sentences.zh: 詔斥其見吳璥辦工遲緩，慮同獲咎，預為地步，褫職，予郎中銜，留河南專司大工錢糧。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked him for seeing Wu Jing's slow progress in the work, fearing shared guilt, and preparing an excuse in advance; he was stripped of office, given the rank of director, and kept in Henan to manage funds for the great works.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked him for seeing Wu Jing's slow progress, fearing shared guilt, and preparing an excuse in advance. He was stripped of office, given the rank of director, and kept in Henan to manage funds for the great works.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，命營山東運河事務，兼署山東巡撫，專駐張秋，籌備趲運事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was ordered to manage Shandong canal affairs, concurrently acting as governor of Shandong, stationed specially at Zhangqiu to prepare urgent transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was ordered to manage Shandong canal affairs and concurrently serve as acting governor of Shandong, stationed at Zhangqiu to prepare urgent transport.

sentences.zh: 尋授安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，調漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was transferred to director-general of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daoguang he was transferred to director-general of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 二年，擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 初，湖廣行銷淮鹽，用封輪法，大商壟斷，小商向隅，甫改開輪，又有跌價爭售之害。

translations.literal: At first Huguang marketed Huai salt under the sealed-rotation method; great merchants monopolized and small merchants were left aside. When it was just changed to open rotation, there was also the harm of price-cutting competition in sales.
translations.idiomatic: At first Huguang marketed Huai salt under the sealed rotation system, which let great merchants monopolize trade while small merchants were shut out. When the system was changed to open rotation, price-cutting competition brought new abuses.

sentences.zh: 鴻賓請設公司，簽商經理，無論鹽船到岸先後，小商隨到隨售，大商按所到各家計引均銷。

translations.literal: Hongbin asked to establish a company managed by contracted merchants: regardless of whether salt ships arrived first or later, small merchants could sell as soon as they arrived, and great merchants would divide sales evenly by quota according to each arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongbin proposed establishing a company managed by contracted merchants. Small merchants could sell as soon as their salt arrived, regardless of order of arrival, while great merchants would divide sales evenly by quota according to each shipment.

sentences.zh: 試行兩月後，販運踴躍，著為令。

translations.literal: After a two-month trial, transport and sales were vigorous, and it was enacted as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: After a two-month trial transport and sales flourished, and the system was enacted as permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 時議折漕以資治河，鴻賓疏言徵收折色，弊竇叢生，莫若令民間完交本色，由州縣賣米易銀，轉解河工，詔以易啟抑勒捏價、加收平色諸弊，未允行。

translations.literal: At the time there was debate on converting tribute grain to fund river works; Hongbin memorialized that collecting commuted payments bred many abuses, and that it would be better to have the people pay in kind, with districts and counties selling grain for silver to remit to river works. An edict held that this would easily give rise to extortion, forced prices, and added surcharges, and it was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was debate on converting tribute grain to fund river works. Li Hongbin memorialized that collecting commuted payments bred many abuses and that it would be better to have the people pay in kind, with districts and counties selling grain for silver to remit to river works. An edict held that this would easily breed extortion, forced prices, and added surcharges, and the proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 調兩廣總督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor-general of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 廣東通商久，號為利藪。

translations.literal: Guangdong had long traded with foreigners and was called a profit nest.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had long traded with foreigners and was known as a nest of profit.

sentences.zh: 自嘉慶以來，英吉利國勢日強，漸跋扈。

translations.literal: Since Jiaqing, England's national power grew daily stronger and gradually became overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jiaqing reign British power had grown steadily stronger and the foreigners had grown increasingly overbearing.

sentences.zh: 故事，十三行洋商有缺，十二家聯保承充，虧帑則攤償。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a vacancy occurred among the thirteen foreign merchants, the twelve firms jointly guaranteed the replacement, and losses to the treasury were shared in repayment.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when a vacancy occurred among the thirteen licensed foreign merchants, the twelve remaining firms jointly guaranteed a replacement, and any loss to the treasury was shared among them.

sentences.zh: 英領事顛地知洋行獲利厚，欲以洋廝容阿華充商，諸商不允，乃賄鴻賓得之。

translations.literal: The English consul Dent knew foreign firms reaped thick profits and wished to install the foreign clerk Rong Ahua as merchant; the merchants would not agree, so he bribed Hongbin and obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: The English consul Dent knew how profitable the foreign trade was and wished to install the foreign clerk Rong Ahua as a licensed merchant. When the other merchants refused, he bribed Li Hongbin and secured the appointment.

sentences.zh: 顛地曰：「吾以為總督若何嚴重，詎消數万金便營私耶！

translations.literal: Dent said: "I thought how grave a governor-general would be—could he be bought for private gain with only a few tens of thousands in gold!
translations.idiomatic: Dent said, "I thought a governor-general would be so formidable—who would have guessed he could be bought for private gain with only a few tens of thousands in gold!

sentences.zh: 」於是始輕中國官吏。

translations.literal: " From this he first looked lightly on Chinese officials.
translations.idiomatic: " From that moment he began to look lightly on Chinese officials.

sentences.zh: 容阿華尋以淫侈耗貲逃，勿獲，官帑無著，不能責諸商代償，乃以抽分法為彌補，眾商藉以漁利，夷情不服，日益多事。

translations.literal: Rong Ahua soon fled after dissolute extravagance exhausted his wealth and could not be captured; official funds had no place to be recovered, and the other merchants could not be charged to repay; a profit-sharing method was then used to make up the loss, the merchants used it to fish for profit, foreign sentiment was dissatisfied, and affairs grew more troublesome daily.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Ahua soon fled after dissolute extravagance exhausted his wealth and could not be captured. With official funds unrecoverable and the other merchants unable to make up the loss, a profit-sharing scheme was adopted as compensation. The merchants used it to enrich themselves, foreign merchants were dissatisfied, and troubles multiplied.

sentences.zh: 鴉片流行日廣，漏銀外洋，鴻賓屢疏陳查禁之法及禁種罌粟，並增築虎門大角砲台，以資控禦，而奉行具文，未有實效。

translations.literal: Opium spread daily wider and silver leaked abroad; Hongbin repeatedly memorialized methods of investigation and prohibition and forbidding cultivation of poppies, and also added fortifications at Humen and Dajiao, to aid control—but implementation was mere form and had no real effect.
translations.idiomatic: Opium spread ever wider and silver drained abroad. Li Hongbin repeatedly memorialized on methods of prohibition and on banning poppy cultivation, and also added fortifications at Humen and Dajiao to strengthen control. But enforcement remained mere form and achieved no real effect.

sentences.zh: 十年，協辦大學士，仍留總督任。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed associate grand secretary while retaining his post as governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed associate grand secretary while remaining governor-general.

sentences.zh: 十一年，崖州黎匪亂，鴻賓駐雷州，令提督劉榮慶、總兵孫得發剿平之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Li bandits of Yazhou rebelled; Hongbin stationed himself at Leizhou and ordered Regional Commander Liu Rongqing and Brigadier Sun Defa to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Li bandits of Yazhou rebelled. Li Hongbin stationed himself at Leizhou and ordered Regional Commander Liu Rongqing and Brigadier Sun Defa to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉光三奏廣東匪徒立會滋擾，鴻賓疏陳：「無三點會名目，惟搶劫打單，勒索民財，根株未絕。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Guangsan memorialized that Guangdong bandits formed societies and caused disturbances; Hongbin memorialized: "There is no society called the Three Dots; there are only robbery and written threats extorting the people's wealth, and the roots are not yet cut.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Guangsan memorialized that Guangdong bandits were forming societies and causing disturbances. Li Hongbin replied: "There is no society called the Three Dots. There are only robbery and written threats extorting the people's wealth, and the roots have not yet been cut.

sentences.zh: 隨時訪拿，準自首免罪。

translations.literal: They are seized whenever found, and those who surrender are permitted to escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: They are seized whenever found, and those who surrender are permitted to escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 請廣、潮、肇、嘉諸府州山場荒地，令無業遊民報墾，永不昇科，庶衣食有資，免流匪僻。

translations.literal: I ask that in the prefectures and departments of Guangzhou, Chaozhou, Zhaoqing, and Jiaying, idle wasteland in the hills be opened to registration by unemployed wanderers, never to be taxed, so that they may have food and clothing and wandering bandits be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that idle wasteland in the hills of Guangzhou, Chaozhou, Zhaoqing, and Jiaying be opened to registration by unemployed wanderers, never to be taxed, so that they may have food and clothing and wandering banditry may be reduced.

sentences.zh: 」如議行。

translations.literal: " This was carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: " This was carried out as proposed.

sentences.zh: 入覲，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He came to audience and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court for audience and was granted the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 十二年春，湖南瑤趙金龍倡亂，廣東連州瑤聞風蠢動，遣兵防剿。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twelfth year the Yao Zhao Jinlong of Hunan raised rebellion; the Yao of Lianzhou in Guangdong stirred at the news, and troops were sent to guard and suppress.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twelfth year the Yao leader Zhao Jinlong rebelled in Hunan. Hearing the news, the Yao of Lianzhou in Guangdong stirred, and troops were sent to guard and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 五月，鴻賓赴連州，三路進兵，雖有斬獲，兵弁傷亡多，疏請俟湖南事竣進剿，詔斥任賊蔓延；

translations.literal: In the fifth month Hongbin went to Lianzhou and advanced on three routes; though there were kills and captures, many officers and soldiers were killed or wounded. He memorialized asking to wait until the Hunan affair was finished before advancing; an edict rebuked him for letting the bandits spread;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Li Hongbin went to Lianzhou and advanced on three routes. Though there were kills and captures, many officers and soldiers were killed or wounded. He memorialized asking to wait until the Hunan rebellion was finished before advancing. An edict rebuked him for letting the rebels spread;

sentences.zh: 提督劉榮慶衰庸，不早糾劾，嚴議革職，改留任。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Liu Rongqing was decrepit and incompetent and had not been impeached early; after strict deliberation he was dismissed from office but changed to retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Liu Rongqing was decrepit and incompetent and had not been impeached in time. After strict deliberation he was dismissed from office but allowed to remain in post.

sentences.zh: 命尚書禧恩等由湖南移師赴粵剿辦，禧恩言：「粵兵多食鴉片，不耐山險，鴻賓陳奏不實。

translations.literal: Minister Xi'en and others were ordered to move troops from Hunan to Guangdong to suppress the affair; Xi'en said: "Guangdong troops mostly eat opium and cannot endure mountain dangers; Hongbin's memorials are not truthful.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xi'en and others were ordered to move troops from Hunan to Guangdong to suppress the rebellion. Xi'en reported: "Guangdong troops mostly use opium and cannot endure mountain terrain. Li Hongbin's memorials are not truthful.

sentences.zh: 」褫職逮治，遣戍烏魯木齊。

translations.literal: " He was stripped of office, arrested and tried, and banished to Urumqi.
translations.idiomatic: " He was stripped of office, arrested and tried, and banished to Urumqi.

sentences.zh: 十四年，釋還，予編修。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was released and restored, and given the rank of compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was released and restored to the rank of Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 家居久之，二十年，卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for a long time and died in the twentieth year.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for many years and died in the twentieth year.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宣宗初政，勵精求治。

translations.literal: The commentary says: At the beginning of the Daoguang reign the emperor strove diligently to seek good government.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: At the beginning of the Daoguang reign the emperor strove diligently to seek good government.

sentences.zh: 孫玉庭、蔣攸銛並以老成膺分陝之寄，大事多以諮決。

translations.literal: Sun Yuting and Jiang Youxian both, by their seasoned maturity, received the trust of frontier appointments, and great affairs were mostly decided after consulting them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yuting and Jiang Youxian both, by their seasoned maturity, received the empire's weightiest frontier appointments, and great affairs were often decided after consulting them.

sentences.zh: 其時鹽、河、漕皆積困，玉庭持重，晚稍模棱。

translations.literal: At that time salt, rivers, and grain transport were all deeply strained; Yuting was steady, but in his later years grew somewhat equivocal.
translations.idiomatic: At that time salt, rivers, and grain transport were all deeply strained. Sun Yuting was steady, but in his later years grew somewhat equivocal.

sentences.zh: 攸銛直行己意，眷注遂衰，然其汲引人才，識量遠矣。

translations.literal: Youxian went straight by his own will, imperial favor therefore declined, yet in drawing up talent his vision was far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Youxian went his own way, and imperial favor therefore declined, yet in promoting talent his vision was far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 李鴻賓初以建言驟起，後乃簠簋不飭，貽海疆隱患。

translations.literal: Li Hongbin at first rose swiftly through remonstrance, but later failed to keep his vessels of office clean and bequeathed hidden troubles on the maritime frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongbin at first rose swiftly through remonstrance, but later failed to keep his conduct clean and bequeathed hidden troubles on the maritime frontier.

sentences.zh: 三人皆不能以功名終，公私之殊，不可概論也。

translations.literal: All three were unable to end their careers with full merit and fame; the difference between public and private conduct cannot be discussed in one breath.
translations.idiomatic: None of the three was able to end his career with full honor. The difference between public service and private conduct cannot be judged by a single measure.
